note: Score cues for the adaptive soundtrack. Committed so a regeneration is reproducible rather than a fishing trip: model, tags, seed, steps and key are the artifact, not just the prompt. Baked by scripts/bake-audio.mjs; raw renders stay gitignored under assets/audio-src/raw/.

musical.why: Owner's direction: sparse, emotional, moving lo-fi instrumental -- not crowded, minimal effects. Camelot 6A is G MINOR, so the major at wheel position 6 is 6B, B flat major, which is 6A's relative major and stays compatible with it either way. 74 bpm is lo-fi tempo: unhurried enough that the quiet scenes breathe, steady enough to anchor a scroll. On 1.5 bpm and keyscale are REAL conditioning inputs rather than prompt hints, which is what retires the old tempoIsAHint caveat.
musical.attack: The percussion must carry ATTACK even though the genre is soft. The scroll has no other rhythmic anchor, and fx.audioPulse drives the halftone breathe off this bus, so a cue with smeared transients gives the visual nothing to move on either. Lo-fi is band-limited and warm AROUND its transients, not mushy through them.
musical.consequence: The quiet valleys (cover, origin, terminal are intensity 1) were designed around a restrained bed. arrangement() in lib/audio/score.ts plays only the 'other' layer at 0.22 gain there, with bass and drums fully out. Worth an ear on the cover and the terminal specifically.

cues.tags: [Instrumental] lo-fi instrumental, sparse minimal trio, felt piano, upright double bass, brushed drum kit, close-miked piano with audible hammer attack, dry rim click, brushed snare with a sharp leading edge, fingertip noise on the bass strings, long silences between phrases, melancholy and hopeful, patient emotional build, dry room, minimal processing, clean defined high end, no pads, no synths, no strings, no guitar, no vocals
cues.promptNotes: The DELETIONS matter as much as the additions. The first cue's tag list carried 'tape saturation', 'warm analog synth pads', 'restrained and patient' and 'noir electronic' -- the first two are literal instructions to remove high frequencies and supply attackless texture, the last two crowd the arrangement. Every surviving descriptor either names an instrument or names an attack.
cues.intent: The single master cue. Demucs splits it into drums / bass / other / vocals; the first three become the vertical layers the scroll mixes. Generating ONE cue is what guarantees the layers share key, tempo and phase -- four separate cues would not line up.

stems.vocalsExpected: near-silent; the cue is instrumental. It came out at -42 dBFS and is simply not listed as a slot -- there is no automatic gate.
stems.mixLaw: Wall-clock locked, gain-mixed by t. NOT scrubbed: real music has rhythmic identity and scrubbing it by scroll position sounds like a turntable. The cue loops on its own clock; only the layer GAINS are a pure function of t and velocity, which is standard game vertical layering and scrub-safe by construction.

modelNotes:
ACE-Step 1.5, NON-XL turbo. Three deliberate choices, each measured:
1.5 over v1: v1's own paper concedes the defect this project measured -- it 'relies on a mel-spectrogram-based DCAE and a 32kHz monophonic vocoder', a hard 16 kHz ceiling with phase discarded and resynthesised, which is the mechanism behind the 40-60 ms smeared transient columns in the first cue. 1.5 is waveform-domain: 48 kHz stereo, 64-channel latent at 25 Hz, so a 40 ms frame grid against v1's ~93 ms mel frames.
NON-XL over XL: XL is 9.29 GB against non-XL's 4.46 GB, and on a 24 GB card that difference is the whole 120 s decode. Measured: XL renders 15 s and 40 s in 21 s wall, then falls off a cliff -- 80 s did not finish in 9 minutes and 120 s ran 140 minutes without writing a byte. Non-XL does the full 120 s in 71 s at 12 GB. Do not 'upgrade' to XL for this duration.
TURBO over base: base at 50 steps measured 8-16 kHz at -33.5 dBFS against 1k-4k at -40.7 -- highs 7 dB LOUDER than the mids, which no acoustic kit does, and its spectrogram shows sustained horizontal bands at ~7 kHz and ~11-13 kHz. That is the GAN shimmer 1.5 is known for, and a sparse mix has nothing to mask it. Turbo at 8 steps has a natural downward slope and clean discrete transients.

measured.crest_2k_8k_dB: 38.6 -> 29.6 (band occupied rather than empty with rare bursts)
measured.topOctaveDeficit: sub sat 39.2 dB above the 4-8k band in v1; 6.9 dB now
measured.format: 48 kHz stereo, exactly 120.000 s (v1 was 44.1 kHz, 119.908 s)
